about: The Benedic, Domine is a short blessing before a meal. Those gathered ask the Lord to bless both them and the gifts they are about to receive from his bounty, making the petition through Christ.

fn.w001: The imperative opens a direct petition to the Lord and governs two coordinated objects: “nos” and “hæc tua dona”.
fn.w002: The vocative identifies the Lord as the prayer's sole addressee.
fn.w003: The first direct object of “Bénedic” comprises the community of speakers.

fn.w004: The conjunction joins persons and gifts as coordinate objects of one blessing.
fn.w005: The demonstrative agrees with “dona” and points to the gifts present at the meal.
fn.w006: The possessive relates the gifts to the Lord addressed in the prayer.
fn.w007: The second direct object of “Bénedic”, coordinated with “nos”.

seg.tr: which we are about to receive from your bounty.

fn.w008: The relative resumes neuter “dona” and serves as the object of the participle “sumptúri” in the predicate with “sumus”.
fn.w009: The preposition with the ablative marks the source of the gifts received.
fn.w011: The ablative after “de” names divine bounty as the source of the gifts.
fn.w012: With “sumptúri”, the auxiliary forms a first-person plural future active periphrastic.
fn.w013: The future active participle agrees with the understood human speakers and, with “sumus”, expresses imminent reception.

fn.w015: The accusative governed by “Per” expresses Christ's mediation in the prayer's conclusion.
fn.w017: The adjective agrees with “Dóminum” and includes the same community that spoke as “nos” and “sumus”.
